Materialize a burn as a dense raster

Source: R/cb_materialize.R
cb_materialize.Rd

Expand the sparse tables of a cb_burn() into a dense cell vector in the layout returned by gdalraster::read_ds(): a plain vector, one element per cell, in row-major order starting at the top-left cell, carrying a "gis" attribute that describes the grid (type, bbox, dim, srs, datatype). This is a stable format definition, so no dependency on 'gdalraster' is needed to produce or consume it, and the result can be handed straight to gdalraster::plot_raster() or wrapped as a matrix with cb_as_matrix().

Usage

cb_materialize(
  x,
  value = c("coverage", "id", "count", "intersects", "interiors_meet", "covers",
    "touches", "covered_by"),
  background = NA
)

Arguments

x

A cb_burn object.

value

What each cell should hold:

"coverage"

(default) summed coverage. Interior run cells contribute 1, boundary cells their fraction, line cells their length (CRS units), points 1 each. Overlapping geometries add, so values above 1 are possible; use pmin(., 1) if a clamped mask is wanted. Output datatype is "Float32".

"id"

the 1-based input position of the geometry covering the cell; where geometries overlap the highest id wins (later inputs are burned over earlier ones). Boundary, line, and point cells count as covered. Output datatype is "Int32".

"count"

the number of distinct geometries with a record in the cell. Output datatype is "Int32".

"intersects", "interiors_meet", "covers", "touches", "covered_by"

the number of polygons satisfying that predicate against the cell, as in cb_cells_where(). Needs a relations table (cb_burn(relate = TRUE) or cb_relate()). "intersects" is the exact all-touched mask: unlike "count" it includes cells a polygon only touches along a wall or at a corner, and cells holding slivers the burn rounds away. Output datatype is "Int32".

background

Value for cells not touched by any geometry. Default NA.

Value

A numeric ("coverage") or integer (every other value) vector of length ncol * nrow with attribute gis, a list: type = "raster", bbox = c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax), dim = c(ncol, nrow, 1), srs (the burn's crs, or ""), and datatype.

Details

Consider cb_crop() first when the parent grid is large and the geometry occupies only part of it.

Affine grids

For a burn from cb_burn_index() the cells are rotated or sheared, which the gis format cannot describe with a bounding box alone. The vector is still in grid order (row-major from the top-left cell, one element per cell), bbox is the bounding box of the grid's outline in world coordinates, and an extra element geotransform holds the six GDAL numbers that define where each cell is. Consumers that only read bbox and dim will place the raster approximately but with square, unrotated cells.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(wk)
sq <- wkt("POLYGON ((2.5 4.5, 6.5 4.5, 6.5 8.5, 2.5 8.5, 2.5 4.5))")
b <- cb_burn(sq, extent = c(0, 10, 0, 10), dimension = c(10, 10))
v <- cb_materialize(b)
cb_as_matrix(v)
} # }
